# `Q-22-10` — Ragged Rows In Math Environment

> The rows of a math environment (`pmatrix`, `aligned`, `cases`, …) do not all have the same number of `&`-separated cells.

## What this means

Matrices and alignments are grids; a short row is padded with empty cells so the grid stays rectangular, and the padding is reported here. The output is usually what was intended, but the padding may hide a missing `&`.

## Why this happens

Common causes: a forgotten `&` in one row, a `\\` that ended a row early, or an extra `&` in one row.

## How to fix it

Give every row the same number of cells, using empty cells (`a & & c`) where a position should stay blank.

## Where it is reported

Math diagnostics point into the `.qmd` at the exact characters inside the
`$…$` or `$$…$$` block, including math that spans several lines or sits
inside a block quote or list item. When a `\newcommand` macro is involved,
a problem inside the macro body points at the definition and a problem in
a macro argument points at the use.
